newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Island Dyeing to issue convertible notes.
newsitem.headline: Island Dyeing to issue convertible notes.

text.p: Island Dyeing and Printing Co Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to issue HK$100 million of convertible notes to repay a short-term bank loan, fund the demolition of a property and for working capital purposes.

The company said in a statement that Gearing International Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Island Dyeing shareholder Sun Hung Kai Hong Kong Industries Ltd, would subscribe in cash for HK$35 million of the principal amount of the notes.
SHK Industries and its associates hold about 35 per cent of the issued share capital of Island Dyeing.

First Pacific Land (HK) Ltd and First Pacific Management Services Ltd would subscribe in cash for HK$16 million and HK$14 million respectively, and independent subscribers Hua Jian International Finance Co Ltd and Garratt Commercial Corp would respectively subscribe for HK$22 million and HK$13 million.
First Pacific Land and First Pacific Davies Ltd (FPD) hold about 16.09 per cent in Island Dyeing.
First Pacific Management, a subsidiary of First Pacific Davies, holds a 13.75 percent stake in Island Dyeing.
Island Dyeing said the notes carry an interest rate of six per cent per annum and the right to convert the principal amount into ordinary shares at an initial conversion price of HK$7.60.
Assuming full conversion, 13.16 million shares would be issued, representing about 19.94 percent and 16.62 percent of the existing and enlarged issued share capital respectively.
The net proceeds of the notes would be used to repay a short-term loan of HK$73.5 million due on December 24, 1996.
Island Dyeing said it is negotiating for a temporary extension of the loan for about one month but no formal agreement has yet been reached.
